newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Disney cut to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Disney cut to hold.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said analyst Alan Kassan downgraded Walt Disney Co to hold from accumulate.
Kassan said he was concerned that its ABC unit will faller deeper into third place in ratings in the upcoming TV season.

He also said that, with the recently strengthened Fox/Liberty Networks, "TV sports rights are going to go through the roof, and that (Disney unit) ESPN will really have to pay up to keep the rights they have."

Kassan said he expects that Disney's new "Hercules" animated feature film "will pick up in the second week," and should generate about $150 million at the box office. "It may not be a blockbuster film, but it will do well."
-- Also, Kassan said that new releases, including "Con Air," and the foreign rights to Viacom Inc's Paramount's "Face/Off," will also help results.
-- Kassan did not change his earnings estimates of $2.70 per share for 1997, and $3.20 for 1998.
-- Kassan said the stock will have some near-term risk. Shares fell 1-5/16 to 77-1/4.

-- Fox/Liberty Networks is a venture of News Corp and Liberty Media Corp, a unit of Tele-Communications Inc. Fox/Liberty last month made a deal with Cablevision Systems Corp that was expected to create a national sports network.
